question: Should OpenClaw allow explicit `gateway.auth.mode="none"` on non-loopback/private-ingress binds, and if so must it use a separate dangerous opt-in instead of relaxing the existing guard?
rationale: The code path is clear, but the requested behavior intentionally changes who can reach powerful Gateway operator surfaces; automation cannot decide that security boundary or product policy.

options.title: Keep current boundary
options.body: Leave non-loopback Gateway binds requiring token, password, or trusted-proxy auth and keep this issue open only if maintainers want to revisit the policy later.

options.title: Design guarded private-ingress opt-in
options.body: Accept the user need but require a named dangerous opt-in, prominent startup/security-audit warnings, docs, and tests before implementation.

options.title: Relax `auth.mode=none` directly
options.body: Allow explicit none mode to satisfy non-loopback startup without a second interlock, accepting the highest exposure risk and relying on external infrastructure.

recommendation.title: Design guarded private-ingress opt-in
recommendation.body: Accept the user need but require a named dangerous opt-in, prominent startup/security-audit warnings, docs, and tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history ties this handle to the current exposed-startup and no-auth security boundaries, making them the best available owner for the security/product decision.
